title: Easy-to-Maintain Flooring for Dining Areas
htmlContent:
Easy-to-Maintain Flooring for Dining Areas

When selecting the best flooring for your dining room, it is a good idea to consider the work that the flooring will have to withstand, as well as how good the floor will look overall when it has been laid. If you intend to have your dining room adjacent to your kitchen,  then you will need to think carefully about the most suitable flooring to use.

Understanding Flooring Options

In order to choose a new floor we need to understand the various forms of flooring that are available,  different types of flooring material has its own strengths and considerations. From traditional hardwoods to contemporary luxury vinyl, the choices are numerous and will affect not only the appearance of thedining area and kitchen but how it feels.  Recognizing the basic differences is the foundation of selecting the most suitable floor.

Types of Flooring Materials

There are a myriad of types of flooring materials to choose from,  with flooring needs, durability and budget in mind. For example, ceramic tile and porcelain tile both make perfect flooring for the kitchen and bathrooms due to their durability and ability to stand water. No matter the budget, vinyl flooring, especially with the luxury vinyl,  is a very versatile and easy to keep clean.

Considering the look of the natural more expensive materials, such as wood or stone flooring, vinyl flooring can easily adopt that look for less all while being a very durable and easy to care for product.

Other options that help to bring the warmth and feel of a wood or stone floor are engineered flooring,  cork flooring, and even highly polished concrete floor.

Durability and Maintenance

Ease of clean-up and durability are the most important attributes when selecting a floor material if in heavy use areas such as a dining room or kitchen.  Any flooring material that may come in heavy use areas such as a dining room or a kitchen should be durable. A durable floor can stand up to heavy traffic, doesn‘t scratch easily and will last longer. You should also be aware of the ease of maintaining the floor as well.  You should know that tiles such as ceramic tiles and vinyl flooring are durable, easy to clean and maintain and ideal floorings for kitchens. With engineered flooring you may need a little more of maintenance than of vinyl.

Affordable Flooring Solutions

Looking for cheap flooring options doesn‘t mean sacrificing style or quality. There are many options for affordable floors. Flooring options like vinyl flooring,  which includes luxury vinyl flooring,  are a quality flooring alternative that are able to replicate the beauty and durability of natural materials like stone or flooring at a cheap price. Laminate flooring is also a cheap flooring alternative that is both durable and easy to clean. Ceramic tile can be also be a pretty cheap flooring option based on the look you‘re going for. This can be a hardwearing and moisture proof flooring for kitchens and dining rooms.

Popular Kitchen Flooring Ideas

Ceramic Tile Flooring

Ceramic tile flooring is very commonly used for kitchens and is one of the most widely used. It is very easy to keep clean and is water resistant. It is easy to maintain and keep clean as well, aiding in the overall hygienic environment of a kitchen. Ceramic tile also comes in an enormous variety of colors and patterns in many shapes and sizes,  so it offers a lot of variety in the kind of style that a kitchen should have; ranging from more natural looking rustic styles to more vibrant modern looking ones. The fact that they are so strong means that they will last for a very long time as a floor and is undoubtedly a very long lasting floor surface.

Vinyl Flooring Options

Vinyl flooring has moved on leaps and bounds and there are now a wide range of stylish and incredibly versatile flooring options suitable for modern kitchens.  The luxury vinyl flooring is remarkably durable and looks completely natural often imitating the stone or wood flooring without the expensive cost or the time-consuming maintenance issues that come with these. Extremely straightforward to look after,  the vinyl flooring types are proofed against water and have a good underfoot feel to them making them popular with the high traffic areas of the kitchen. Due to the different designs and cheap prices, it is one of the best choices.

Engineered Wood for Dining Areas

Engineered wood flooring can be a good compromise for those who want the warmth and natural looks of wood in a dining area,  especially open plan kitchen and dining areas.  Engineered wood is an excellent way to have the look and feel of solid flooring,  but also needs greater stability and the moisture and temperature fluctuations may have less of an effect on the flooring if it is not as water resistant as other floor types such as ceramic tile and vinyl. However some engineered wood types can be a good choice, but will need regular maintenance and be sealed well. It can provide a more luxurious look to the interior, as well as creating a more comfortable surface under foot.

Choosing the Best Flooring for High-Traffic Areas

Floors of high traffic zones like the kitchen, dining area,  corridors need to be both durable and attractive. One needs to consider various aspects before finalizing the best floor for these high traffic zones such as durability, ease of maintenance, wear,  tear resistance etc. A durable floor proves both practical and hygienic.  One has to consider these points while selecting the flooring material.

Durable Flooring Materials

Regarding flooring materials for high-traffic areas that will stand up to heavy foot traffic, several materials are known for their durability. Ceramic tiles and porcelain tiles are two materials ranked as the best kitchen floors because they are quite hard and resistant to damage from water,  spills,  and stains. Luxury vinyl flooring would be a durable choice; it often would look like more high-end natural materials such as wood or stone flooring but hold up better than the natural materials. Engineered wood flooring would also be durable for a high-traffic area, with the condition that its resistance to water is good. These materials are all known for their durability.

Cork Flooring Benefits

Cork flooring has a unique combination of some great advantages and is becoming more popular in rooms for moderate traffic.  Its great advantage is the comfort under foot due to its natural bounce and “cushioning”. It is a great environmentally friendly flooring material which can be very resilient and durable when sealed and is also very straight forward to look after.  It has a natural water resistance and insulation qualities which can contribute to energy efficiency and is a soft material to walk on. Although it might not be the best choice for a bathroom or very wet room without sealing it is a fashionable and kind to the environment flooring choice which could be great for a dining room due to its soft, warm and insulating qualities.

Restaurant Flooring Considerations

Commercial kitchen flooring is a somewhat specialized topic because of the very specific considerations which must be made in the design of a restaurant or kitchen. While many other spaces in a typical building have relatively minimal concerns for durability and ease of cleaning,  restaurants and commercial kitchens must use the best possible flooring to withstand the wear and tear of multiple customers,  spills, and regular cleaning in accordance with health codes. The best flooring options in a commercial restaurant kitchen vary, but traditionally have been ceramic, quarry tile, and some vinyl options (primarily commercial grade luxury vinyl products) for their water resistance, slip resistance,  and ease of cleaning.

Flooring Installation and Design

Latest Flooring Trends

The world of flooring is an ever-changing one, with new trends popping up and a perfect marriage of beauty and practicality on offer,  it is an exciting time to be browsing for flooring ideas for the modern home.  One of the most common trends in a variety of flooring mediums is the over-sized floor tile,  with a trend for large format ceramic tile and porcelain tile in a range of natural and neutral hues, and a very consistent trend for creating single unit floor designs that stretch as far as the eye can see. In kitchens and open plan dining room areas, this effect creates a seamless feeling of space, making even small rooms appear spacious.  Another current popular trend is a towards natural materials (or a hyper-realistic imitation of natural materials), with luxury vinyl flooring among the leading products in imitating a consistent range of multiple variations of hardwood flooring and stone flooring. With an increased focus on sustainability and eco-friendliness, there is also a clear trend towards cork flooring and bamboo flooring both of which can make very durable and low-maintenance flooring choices.

Floor Design Ideas for Kitchens

There are many kitchen floor ideas and imagination is the only limit. For a ultramodern look, polished concrete floor will give that clean, industrial feel, yet be extremely durable and easy to clean while large slab ceramic tile offers a clean finish that also is easy to maintain.  If warmth is more desirable then engineered wood flooring comes in many tones and finishes providing that elegant look of hardwood that is more resistant to the effects of moisture. For a less expensive floor that simply looks like the real thing then luxury vinyl flooring is a great option, it will create any intricate pattern possible using any “natural” materials but at a lot less cost. The best flooring for kitchens is not only going to relate well to the cabinet and counter tops but also functional,  hardwearing and water resistant.

Installation Tips for Easy Maintenance

When it comes to upkeep and durability, the key to the tile, porcelain, vinyl, or engineered wood‘s longevity is a good install. Whether it is ceramic tile,  porcelain tile,  or even vinyl flooring, the tiles should be sealed and grouted carefully to prevent water intrusion and for easy upkeep, not to mention sanitation.  Vinyl flooring,  if it is le luxury vinyl,  should be installed on a perfectly level subfloor as any waves or dips will catch dirt and cause premature wear. Engineered wood floors should be installed with the correct adhesive, and the wood must be properly acclimated prior to installation or heaving may occur, not to mention a high quality sealant can be put down on the floor increasing water resistance. Professionally installed floor will help prevent many common problems and keep the homeowner happy with their durable selection,  with minimal effort for years to come.
